$comment: Contract v4 DRAFT for user approval. Superset of v3 with local-lane observability certification. Every new allocation and budget ceiling is provisional pending the non-certifying fault and observability smoke; no evidence may be certified until a separate approval receipt binds the final bytes.

managed.observabilityApplicability: not-applicable; retains the v3 item set

timeline.membership: scheduled time in half-open [T0, T0+steadySeconds); T0 fixed only after both machines ready and warmup done; faults never overlap steady or each other's recovery

applicability.managed: not-applicable; evaluate exactly the inherited v3 item set

backlog.claim: certifies the aged-queue metric, alert and recovery under controlled delivery scheduling; does not certify natural retry backoff under a partition

calibration.databaseCpuPercentDefinition: baseline-subtracted incremental database CPU-seconds over each probe window at the combined two-machine rate (2 probes per 15 seconds), divided by actual elapsed window seconds and recorded database CPU quota
calibration.successfulPathWireStatementDerivation: 45 successful application queries x 2 wire statements for signalled PID preflight plus query. Outside runtime schema readiness: health 4, migration 1, metrics 2, queue 1, statements context 1 + mapping probes 14 + counter read 1 = 24 application queries / 48 wire statements. verifyPostgreSqlRuntimeSchema reaches 21 executor.query sites: server readiness; role policy; extension catalog; pg_stat_statements probe; content collation; extension functions; extension operator; GIN operator class; direct GIN operators; indirect GIN operators; GIN support functions; search configuration; migration history; ownership; schema definitions; identity functions; schema ACL; relation ACL; column ACL; function ACL; effective privileges = 21 application queries / 42 wire statements. Total 90. A conditional idle-connection SELECT 1 is excluded and bounded separately at one per acquired connection. Provisional until smoke confirms pg_stat_statements accounting.

workload.identityRule: expected and actual attempt identities are equal; zero unexpected failures

privacy.shortValueRule: values shorter than 8 characters are scanned only as boundary-delimited tokens

actions.unavailable: Run `lcm doctor` and review the storage configuration.
actions.poolFailed: Check backend connectivity, then run `lcm doctor` again.
actions.poolSaturated: Reduce concurrent database load or raise `storage.postgresql.poolMax`, then run `lcm doctor`.
actions.migrationBehind: Run `lcm postgres migrate` with the migration role, then run `lcm doctor`.
actions.migrationAhead: Upgrade LCM to a release that includes every applied migration, then run `lcm doctor`.
actions.migrationDrift: Restore the packaged PostgreSQL schema history; never edit applied migrations.
actions.extensions: Have a database administrator install or update the required PostgreSQL extensions and verify their schema and preload configuration, then run `lcm doctor`.
actions.quarantine: Inspect with `lcm events quarantine` and replay with `lcm events replay <event-id>`.
actions.backlog: Check daemon delivery with `lcm events status`, then run `lcm doctor`.

schedulePerMachine.hook: T0+1+10j, j=0..599; kind [user-prompt,post-tool,post-tool,post-tool][j mod 4]; session s(j mod 4)
schedulePerMachine.sessionSnapshot: T0+30+60k, k=0..99; session s0; hook_event_name Stop; owned pinned Codex transcript fixture
schedulePerMachine.compact: T0+55+300k, k=0..19; session s0; explicit /compact operation; the only compaction source

workload.primaryTextLength: cycle[floor(j/4) mod 4]; ASCII; JSON envelope bytes recorded separately; stored truncation (DATA_SOFT_CAP) recorded, not counted as input change

fixtures.userPrompt: "Always prefer deterministic records. " + lowercase x padding to N bytes; extracts exactly one decision event
fixtures.postTool: tool_name TaskCreate, tool_input {subject: "fixture " + x padding to N bytes, status: "created"}, tool_response "ok"; extracts exactly one task_create event; synthetic compatibility fixture, not native Codex tool proof
fixtures.cardinalityCheck: unit tests for all 8 kind/length combinations; runtime asserts exactly one new row per invocation

emission.productionSettings: batch 100 and 300 s sweep unchanged; drain lease is per machine; sweep timestamps recorded, no collision gate

oracle.invocationLedger: persist invocation id/kind/session/expected count before each serialized hook; capture exactly one new matching row (uuid, machine sequence, source/type/session, scrubbed payload hash) within 2 s after exit; persisted outside SQLite immediately; rows from failed commands reconciled
oracle.captureFailure: workload failure / incomplete, never zero loss

observer.access: direct read-only SQLite (WAL siblings intact); no repository wrapper, no publication lock, no long transaction, no checkpoint/migration
observer.identityCheck: file and parent identity; replacement => incomplete

oracle.acknowledgedPredicate: delivery_state='acknowledged' AND remote_inbox_id IS NOT NULL AND acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL
oracle.lagClock: observer first-seen monotonic minus hook success monotonic; max(0, ...) with raw ordering retained

hookCommandMs.definition: public CLI process start to exit wall time (monotonic); schedule delay reported separately
hookCommandMs.basis: recalibrated from non-certifying smoke-44/45/47 observations (p50 428-441 ms, p95 ~1011 ms) with margin; approval-selected policy limits

acknowledgmentLagSeconds.note: conservative upper bound; exact applied_at not claimed

loss.rule: every successful invocation maps to exactly one oracle event and every oracle event is acknowledged by end of final drain; missing input row and missing ack reported separately

duplicates.gated: zero event ids observed with more than one distinct acknowledged inbox id
duplicates.nonClaim: historical duplicate logical effects / exactly-once (owned by #631)

finalDrain.rule: every oracle event acknowledged and remote_pruned_at non-null; zero nonterminal or awaiting-prune rows; physical deletion not required

recovery.windowRule: sliding [u,u+60s) with u >= clearedAt, evaluated every 1 s once all constituent scheduled operations are terminal; search and store separately; successes >= ceil(0.9*n), n>0; scheduled-time denominators; timeouts are failures; an unaffected machine never masks an affected one

partition.subject: machine A
partition.clearedAt: network restoration verified to same endpoint

restartDatabase.subject: both machines
restartDatabase.clearedAt: fresh SQL/TLS connection to the same owned database verified

recovery.faultWorkload: deterministic rates continue, tagged fault workload; excluded from steady populations; included in loss reconciliation

capacity.configuredPerMachine: 2 persistent daemon runtimes + <=1 transient runtime = 6, cap 8
capacity.evidence: simultaneous-instance maxima enforced; sampled pg_stat_activity peaks (role + client address) as corroboration; record max_connections and reserved slots

clock.method: bracket t0/server/t1 at start, every 60 s, end
clock.localNote: shared host clock; no independent-clock claim; no gated metric subtracts machine and database clocks

diagnosticsNotGated.databaseGrowth: after-minus-before total bytes of lcm schema relations over steady, with submitted bytes

calculations.percentile: nearest-rank: ascending successful samples at index ceil(q*n)-1
calculations.population: pooled across both machines within one lane run; never across lanes or repetitions
calculations.errorRate: nonInjected failed attempts / scheduled steady attempts
calculations.verdict: pass only if every gated item passes on every lane run; a definite breach => fail (takes precedence); otherwise any missing/insufficient evidence => incomplete

repetitions.rationale: bounded baseline observation; not a provider reliability certification
